items.name: storage/get
items.summary: Read one entry from the plugin's **APS** (Anna Persistent Storage) KV namespace — small JSON state keyed by `(scope, key)`. Missing keys resolve to `{value: None, exists: False}` instead of raising.
items.signature: get(*, scope: str = 'tool', key: str) -> dict

params.name: scope
params.summary: ACL scope. Defaults to `tool` (per-Executa namespace).
notes: `tool` — visible only to invocations of this Executa for this user (recommended default).
`app` — shared across all Executas owned by the same anna-app for this user.
`user` — user-global; access requires the host to have minted a `storage_token` whose `allowed_scopes` claim contains `user`.
The Agent's minted `storage_token` is what actually gates access; this argument selects the row family.

params.name: key
params.summary: Entry key within the active scope (≤ 1024 chars).
notes: Namespaced by `(scope, owner, key)` in Postgres — no global collision with other plugins.
Choose stable, opaque keys (e.g. `prefs.v1`, `cursor.gmail.inbox`); the page caches by exact key.

returns.desc:
**On hit** — every field below is present:
• `value: Any` — the stored JSON value
• `exists: True` — injected client-side
• `etag: str` — pass to `storage/set(if_match=...)` for CAS
• `generation: int` — monotonic per-key write counter
• `size_bytes: int` — serialised size of `value`
• `metadata: dict`, `tags: list[str]` — as last written
• `updated_at: str` — ISO-8601 timestamp

**On miss** — Nexus 404 is normalised to `{value: None, exists: False, etag: None}`. `STORAGE_ERR_NOT_FOUND` is never raised.

Always branch on `exists`, not on `value`'s truthiness — a stored `None`, `0`, `[]`, or `""` is a legitimate hit.

errors.name: STORAGE_ERR_NOT_GRANTED
errors.desc: Agent did not mint a storage_token for this invoke.

errors.name: STORAGE_ERR_INVALID_REQUEST
errors.desc: Required field (key/path) missing or wrong type.

errors.name: STORAGE_ERR_NOT_FOUND
errors.desc: Key/path does not exist (normalised on `get`).

errors.name: STORAGE_ERR_PRECONDITION_FAILED
errors.desc: if_match ETag did not match current generation.

errors.name: STORAGE_ERR_QUOTA_EXCEEDED
errors.desc: User APS quota exhausted.

errors.name: STORAGE_ERR_UPSTREAM
errors.desc: Nexus REST returned a non-success status.

items.example:
# Inside an Executa plugin (executa_sdk).
from executa_sdk import ctx

async def append_recent(item_id: str) -> list[str]:
    cur = await ctx.storage.get(key="recent.v1")
    recent = cur["value"] if cur["exists"] else []
    recent = ([item_id] + [x for x in recent if x != item_id])[:20]
    # Optimistic CAS using the etag we just read.
    await ctx.storage.set(
        key="recent.v1",
        value=recent,
        if_match=cur["etag"],  # None on first write is accepted
    )
    return recent
limitations: Value must be JSON-serialisable and ≤ **256 KB** per entry (enforced by `KVSetRequest`). For larger or binary payloads use `files/upload.begin` + `files/upload.complete`.
Backed by Postgres JSONB — **not** a low-latency cache. Read-heavy hot keys (>~50 rps per key) should be memoised in plugin process memory between invokes.
No server-side sub-document selection: the full `value_json` blob is returned. Keep entries small or split into multiple keys keyed by sub-document.
Reads are linearisable per-key but **not** snapshot-consistent across keys — if you need a multi-key atomic view, store them under a single key as a nested object.

Requires the manifest permission `storage.read`. Per-scope access (`user` / `app` / `tool`) is gated by the `storage_token`'s `allowed_scopes` claim, set by the host at install-time grant; the Agent refuses to mint a token for unallowed scopes.

items.name: storage/set
items.summary: Write one entry to the plugin's **APS** KV namespace — full-document replace, ETag-versioned, optionally CAS-guarded by `if_match` and auto-expiring via `ttl_seconds`.
items.signature: set(*, scope: str = 'tool', key: str, value: Any, if_match: str | None = None, metadata: dict | None = None, tags: list[str] | None = None, ttl_seconds: int | None = None) -> dict

params.name: scope
params.summary: ACL scope. Defaults to `tool` (per-Executa namespace).
notes: `tool` / `app` / `user` — same semantics as `storage/get`.
Requires manifest `storage.write`. Per-scope access is gated by the `storage_token`'s `allowed_scopes` claim (`user` / `app` / `tool`).

params.name: key
params.summary: Entry key within the active scope (1–1024 chars).
notes: Namespaced by `(scope, owner, key)`; no global collision with other plugins.
Validated by `validate_kv_key` server-side; rejected as `STORAGE_ERR_INVALID_REQUEST` on empty/oversize.

params.name: value
params.summary: JSON-serialisable payload. **Replaces** the previous value verbatim.
notes: Serialised by `_serialize_value` to canonical UTF-8 JSON; the byte length must be ≤ 256 KB.
There is no server-side merge / JSON-patch — to update a sub-field, do read → mutate → set with `if_match`.
ETag is `sha256(payload)[:32]`, so writing the same value twice yields the same ETag but still bumps `generation`.

params.name: if_match
params.summary: Optimistic concurrency token. Pass the `etag` you previously read.
notes: Mismatch → `STORAGE_ERR_PRECONDITION_FAILED` (HTTP 412); quota reservation is rolled back.
`None` (default) is unconditional write — last-writer-wins. Use only for keys you know are single-writer.
First-time create: pass `None`; there is no separate `if-none-match` mode.

params.name: metadata
params.summary: Opaque per-entry metadata. **Overwrites** the stored dict; not a merge.
notes: Stored on the row and echoed back by `storage/get` and `storage/list`; never used by the server for routing or filtering.
Passing `None` is treated as `{}` on write — i.e. it clears existing metadata.

params.name: tags
params.summary: Up to 32 short labels for client-side filtering.
notes: Surfaced in `storage/list` items so callers can sort/filter without re-reading values.
`None` keeps no tags; an empty list also clears.

params.name: ttl_seconds
params.summary: Auto-expire after N seconds (1 .. 31_536_000, i.e. 1 second to 1 year).
notes: Stored as an absolute `expires_at` timestamp; expired entries are filtered out of `get`/`list` (lazy delete).
Omit (`None`) for permanent state. Updating an existing entry **replaces** `expires_at` — pass it on every write if you want a sliding TTL.

returns.desc:
**`{etag, generation, size_bytes}`** — only these three fields:
• `etag: str` — new sha256 prefix; feed back into the next `if_match`.
• `generation: int` — incremented by 1 on every successful write (creation starts at 1).
• `size_bytes: int` — serialised payload size as accounted against user quota.

Note: `value` / `metadata` / `tags` / `updated_at` are **not** echoed — re-read with `storage/get` if you need them.

limitations: Payload must be JSON-serialisable and ≤ **256 KB** after canonical serialisation. For larger or binary blobs use `files/upload.begin` + `files/upload.complete`.
Full-document replace only — no server-side patch / merge / array-append. Concurrent writers to the same key must use `if_match` to avoid lost updates.

Write path takes a Postgres row lock (`SELECT … FOR UPDATE`) and deducts user quota (Redis Lua + DB fallback). Sustained > ~50 writes/s on a single key will contend; shard hot state across multiple keys.
`metadata` and `tags` are **replace-only** — there is no partial update. Re-send the full desired value each write.
TTL is enforced lazily on read; expired-but-not-yet-deleted entries still occupy quota briefly. A reaper job sweeps them; do not rely on TTL for security-critical wipes.
Requires manifest permission `storage.write`. Per-scope access (`user` / `app` / `tool`) is gated by the `storage_token`'s `allowed_scopes` claim, set by the host at install-time grant.

items.name: storage/delete
items.summary: Soft-delete one entry from the plugin's **APS** KV namespace. The row stays in Postgres (recoverable), but quota is released immediately and subsequent `storage/get`/`storage/list` treat the key as gone.
items.signature: delete(*, scope: str = 'tool', key: str, if_match: str | None = None) -> dict

params.name: scope
params.summary: ACL scope — same semantics as `storage/get` (`tool` / `app` / `user`).
notes: Requires manifest `storage.write`. Per-scope access is gated by the `storage_token`'s `allowed_scopes` claim (`user` / `app` / `tool`).

params.name: key
params.summary: Exact key to delete within the active scope (1–1024 chars).
notes: Exact match only — there is no glob / prefix delete. To bulk-remove, page through `storage/list(prefix=…)` and call `delete` per key.
Validated by `validate_kv_key`; empty or oversize → `STORAGE_ERR_INVALID_REQUEST`.

params.name: if_match
params.summary: Optional CAS guard. Pass the `etag` from your last read to avoid deleting a key that was updated in between.
notes: Mismatch → `STORAGE_ERR_PRECONDITION_FAILED` (HTTP 412); the row is **not** touched.
`None` is an unconditional delete — only safe for keys you know are single-writer.

returns.desc:
**`{deleted: True}`** — synthesised by the SDK from Nexus's `{ok: true}` envelope.

Always returns `deleted=True` on success; the response carries no etag/generation (the row is tombstoned, not rewritten).

limitations: Deleting a missing key raises `STORAGE_ERR_NOT_FOUND` — unlike `storage/get`, 404 is **not** normalised. Wrap in try/except if you are not sure the key exists, or check via `storage/get` first.

Soft delete only — the row is flagged `is_deleted=True`, kept for audit/recovery. Quota is released right away, but the data is not physically purged until a reaper job runs. Do not rely on `delete` as a security-grade wipe.
No bulk / glob delete. Iterate `storage/list(prefix=…)` + `storage/delete` to clear a namespace; expect O(n) round-trips.
Takes a Postgres row lock (`SELECT … FOR UPDATE`). Concurrent deletes on the same key serialise — the second one will see `STORAGE_ERR_NOT_FOUND`.
Requires manifest `storage.write`. Per-scope access is gated by the `storage_token`'s `allowed_scopes` claim (`user` / `app` / `tool`).

items.name: storage/list
items.summary: Enumerate the plugin's **APS** KV keys (alphabetical, cursor-paginated). Returns metadata heads only — `value` is **not** included; re-read with `storage/get` for any key you actually need.
items.signature: list(*, scope: str = 'tool', prefix: str = '', cursor: str | None = None, limit: int = 100) -> dict

params.name: scope
params.summary: ACL scope — same semantics as `storage/get` (`tool` / `app` / `user`).
notes: Listing is per-scope; the same key in `tool` and `app` is reported separately if you list each scope.
Requires manifest `storage.read`. Per-scope access is gated by the `storage_token`'s `allowed_scopes` claim (`user` / `app` / `tool`).

params.name: prefix
params.summary: Filter keys that start with this string. Empty = list everything in the scope.
notes: Forward-match only — no glob or regex. Matching is byte-wise on the raw key.
Validated like a key path: ≤ 1024 chars, no leading `/`, no `.` / `..` segments, no forbidden characters.
Trailing `/` is allowed (e.g. `prefix='cursor/'`); empty trailing segments are tolerated.

params.name: cursor
params.summary: Opaque continuation token returned by a previous call as `next_cursor`.
notes: Encodes the last-seen key; pages walk strict ascending order (`path > cursor`).
Treat as opaque — do not parse, persist long-term, or share across scopes/prefixes.
Pass `None` (or omit) for the first page.

params.name: limit
params.summary: Page size, 1 .. 1000 (default 100).
notes: Out-of-range values are silently clamped by the server (`max(1, min(limit, 1000))`).
The server fetches `limit + 1` rows to decide whether `next_cursor` is set; cost is O(limit).

returns.desc:
**`{items: [...], next_cursor: str | None}`**

Each item is a **head only**:
• `key: str` — the entry key
• `etag: str` — current ETag; reuse for `if_match` writes/deletes
• `size_bytes: int` — serialised value size
• `metadata: dict`, `tags: list[str] | None` — as last written
• `updated_at: str` — ISO-8601 timestamp

`next_cursor` is `None` on the final page. There is **no** total count and **no** `value` field — call `storage/get` for entries you actually want to read.

errors.desc: Agent did not mint a storage_token for this invoke.

errors.name: STORAGE_ERR_INVALID_REQUEST
errors.desc: Required field (key/path) missing or wrong type.

errors.name: STORAGE_ERR_NOT_FOUND
errors.desc: Key/path does not exist (normalised on `get`).

errors.name: STORAGE_ERR_PRECONDITION_FAILED
errors.desc: if_match ETag did not match current generation.

errors.name: STORAGE_ERR_QUOTA_EXCEEDED

errors.name: STORAGE_ERR_UPSTREAM

limitations: Heads only — `value` is never returned. Listing then reading N entries is N+1 round-trips. Keep frequently-co-read state in a single key when possible.
Ordering is strict ascending `key`. No reverse iteration, no order-by-updated_at, no random sample.
No server-side filtering by `tags`, `metadata`, or `size_bytes` — fetch and filter client-side.
Hard page size cap of 1000. Full enumeration of a large namespace requires looping on `next_cursor`; expect O(n / page_size) round-trips.
Soft-deleted entries are excluded; expired (TTL-past) entries are excluded lazily.
Result is a point-in-time view per page — concurrent writes/deletes between pages can cause an entry to appear twice or be skipped. For exact snapshots, write a single key containing an index.
Requires manifest `storage.read`. Per-scope access is gated by the `storage_token`'s `allowed_scopes` claim (`user` / `app` / `tool`).

items.name: files/upload_begin
items.summary: Phase 1 of the two-phase Files (object) upload — reserves an APS object entry (marked `__pending=true`), soft-deducts the declared `size_bytes` from the user's APS quota, and returns a short-lived presigned PUT URL into APS object storage. The plugin then `PUT`s the bytes directly to that URL and calls `files/upload_complete` to flip the entry from pending to durable.
items.signature: uploadbegin(*, scope: Literal['user','app','tool'] = 'app', path: str, size_bytes: int, content_type: str | None = None, metadata: dict[str, str] | None = None, timeout: float = 60.0) -> dict

params.name: scope
params.summary: ACL scope. Files namespace defaults to `app` (shared across the anna-app's tools).
notes: `tool` — visible only to invocations of this Executa for this user.
`app` — shared across all Executas owned by the same anna-app for this user (recommended for files the user-visible app surfaces, e.g. attachments).
`user` — user-global; intended for files the user uploaded via the Anna chat UI. Reading these requires the storage_token's `allowed_scopes` claim to contain `user`.
The Agent's minted `storage_token` is what actually gates access; this argument selects the row family. Unauthorised scope → `STORAGE_ERR_NOT_GRANTED` (`-32021`).

params.name: path
params.summary: Logical file path within the chosen scope (e.g. `reports/2026/q1.pdf`).
notes: Validated server-side by `validate_path`: 1..1024 chars, relative (no leading `/`), segments are non-empty and not `.` / `..`, no ASCII control chars / backslashes / zero-width / BiDi control characters; segments may not start/end with whitespace.
Invalid → `STORAGE_ERR_INVALID_PATH` (`-32027`). The returned path is canonicalised (redundant `/` collapsed) and used verbatim as the APS object key.
Namespaced by `(scope, owner, path)`; collisions with other plugins/users are impossible.

Re-using an existing path is allowed — the row is row-locked (`SELECT … FOR UPDATE`) and rewritten in place; pass `if_match` (server-side only — not exposed by the SDK) to guard against concurrent writers.

params.name: size_bytes
params.summary: Declared byte length of the upload (0 .. 256 MB).
notes: Hard cap is `OBJECT_MAX_BYTES = 256 * 1024 * 1024`. Exceed → `STORAGE_ERR_VALUE_TOO_LARGE` (`-32025`, HTTP 413). Zero-byte uploads are accepted.

Used to **soft-reserve** quota (`storage_quota_service.reserve(soft=True, ttl_seconds=600)`). Only the *delta* over an existing entry's `size_bytes` is reserved; pure overwrites of the same size cost nothing.
The reservation is auto-released by Redis after 10 min if `files/upload_complete` never lands; the row's `__pending` flag stays until a reaper cleans it.
Reservation failure → `STORAGE_ERR_QUOTA_EXCEEDED` (`-32024`); the call rolls back before any presign happens.
Honour the value you declare — APS object storage accepts any size and `files/upload_complete` writes the **actual** size, but quota accounting is based on this number until finalize reconciles.

params.name: content_type
params.summary: MIME type of the upload. **Effectively required** despite the optional Python type.
notes: The Nexus body schema (`_FilesInitBody`) declares `content_type: str` as required (max 120 chars). Omitting it from the SDK call ⇒ FastAPI 422 surfaced as `STORAGE_ERR_INVALID_REQUEST` (`-32028`); empty/oversize ⇒ `STORAGE_ERR_INVALID_PATH` (`-32027`).

Echoed into the presigned URL's signed `Content-Type` query parameter — your subsequent `PUT` **must** send the same `Content-Type` header (the response's `headers` dict supplies it) or APS rejects the upload with 403 SignatureDoesNotMatch.

Stored on the row and surfaced by `files/list` / `files/download_url`. Pick something the consumer will use to choose a viewer (e.g. `application/pdf`, `image/png`); browsers also honour it on signed GETs unless `disposition` overrides.

params.name: metadata
params.summary: Opaque per-entry metadata. **Replaces** the stored dict (no merge).
notes: Server adds `__pending=True` and, when a soft reservation is taken, `__reservation_token=<…>` to the dict before persisting; both are stripped by `files/upload_complete`. Do not use keys starting with `__`.
Echoed back by `files/list` and `storage/get` (for objects). Never used by the server for routing or filtering.
Passing `None` is treated as `{}` on write — it clears any metadata the previous version of the entry carried.

params.name: timeout
params.summary: SDK-side per-call deadline in seconds (default 60s).
notes: Client-side only — the Agent → Nexus hop has its own 15s `request_timeout_s` (`DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_S` in the Anna Agent runtime). Bumping the SDK timeout does not lift the upstream HTTP timeout.
On expiry the call raises the SDK's RPC timeout error, not a storage error.

returns.desc:
Verbatim `PresignedPut` body from Nexus — every field is always present:
• `upload_id: str` — the `aps_entries.uuid` of the (newly created or reused) pending row. **Treat as opaque**; not currently required by `files/upload_complete` (which keys off `path` + `etag`) but handy as a correlation id for logs.
• `put_url: str` — presigned `PUT` URL into APS object storage. Lives for `ttl_seconds` (default **300 s**, Nexus-controlled — the SDK does not expose `ttl_seconds`). Single-use semantically; issuing a second `files/upload_begin` for the same path rewrites the row and invalidates any earlier URL.
• `headers: dict[str, str]` — currently `{"Content-Type": <content_type>}`. **Send these exact headers** with your `PUT` or APS rejects the signature. Future versions may add additional signed transport headers; treat as an opaque set, do not append your own.
• `expires_at: str` — ISO-8601 wall-clock expiry of the URL (= server `utcnow()` + `ttl_seconds`). After this point the `PUT` returns 403 and you must call `files/upload_begin` again.
• `r2_key: str` — APS-internal storage key for this entry (opaque, server-assigned, namespaced by user / scope / entry). Diagnostic only — you do not need it for the `PUT` (it's already baked into `put_url`) and the value is not stable API.

items.example:
# Two-phase Files upload: begin → PUT to presigned URL → complete.
import httpx
from executa_sdk import ctx

async def upload_report(local_path: str, dest: str = "reports/q1.pdf") -> str:
    blob = open(local_path, "rb").read()

    # 1. Reserve quota + get a presigned PUT URL.
    info = await ctx.storage.files.upload_begin(
        path=dest,
        size_bytes=len(blob),
        content_type="application/pdf",
        scope="app",          # default; explicit for clarity
    )

    # 2. PUT the bytes straight to the presigned URL — bypasses the agent host.
    async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=60.0) as http:
        r = await http.put(info["put_url"], content=blob, headers=info["headers"])
        r.raise_for_status()                       # 200/204 on success
        obj_etag = r.headers["etag"].strip('"')  # APS object ETag

    # 3. Tell APS the upload landed — flips __pending=False, finalises quota.
    entry = await ctx.storage.files.upload_complete(
        path=dest,
        etag=obj_etag,
        size_bytes=len(blob),
    )
    return entry["path"]   # durable, listable, downloadable
limitations: **Two-phase, plugin-driven**: nothing is durably stored until `files/upload_complete` succeeds. If your process crashes between begin and complete, the row remains `__pending=true` and the soft quota reservation expires after 10 minutes — a reaper eventually deletes the orphan. Do not skip `upload_complete`.

**`put_url` TTL is capped at 1 h** (`OBJECT_PRESIGN_TTL_MAX = 3600`); the default is **5 min** and the SDK does not let you change it. For large uploads stream the bytes immediately after begin and finalize on the same call site.

**`content_type` is effectively mandatory** even though typed as `Optional[str]` on the SDK. Omitting it surfaces as `STORAGE_ERR_INVALID_REQUEST` from the FastAPI body validator. Always pass a real MIME type.

**`ttl_seconds`, `tags`, `if_match` are not exposed by the Python SDK** (`FilesClient.upload_begin`). The underlying Nexus endpoint accepts them; if you need them, call the REST endpoint directly with the minted `storage_token`.
**Object size cap is 256 MB** (`OBJECT_MAX_BYTES`). For larger payloads you must chunk them across multiple paths yourself — there is no server-side multipart upload.

**Quota is soft-reserved up front** based on the *declared* `size_bytes`. Declaring a much larger value than you actually upload temporarily inflates `used_bytes` until finalize reconciles or the 10-min reservation expires.

**Rewriting an existing path is a full replace** — the previous APS object is overwritten (the entry is re-used; `generation` bumps; etag is replaced). No version history is kept. Use distinct paths if you need historical revisions.

Requires manifest permission `storage.write` and an install-time grant that allows the selected `scope`. The Agent will refuse to mint a `storage_token` with disallowed scopes; calls then fail with `STORAGE_ERR_NOT_GRANTED` (`-32021`).

items.name: files/upload_complete
items.summary: Phase 2 of the two-phase Files (object) upload — APS verifies that the bytes landed against the entry reserved by `files/upload_begin`, replaces the placeholder ETag with the canonical APS-computed object ETag, reconciles `size_bytes` against the actual uploaded size (positive delta is hard-deducted from quota, negative delta is refunded), strips the `__pending` flag, and returns the durable `ObjectEntry`.
items.signature: uploadcomplete(*, scope: Literal['user','app','tool'] = 'app', path: str, etag: str | None = None, size_bytes: int | None = None, content_type: str | None = None, timeout: float = 60.0) -> dict

params.name: scope
params.summary: ACL scope. **Must match** the scope you used at `upload_begin` (rows are scoped).
notes: Mismatched scope → `STORAGE_ERR_NOT_FOUND` (row lookup fails); the pending row in the original scope still expires after 10 min and is reaped.
Per-scope authorisation is enforced by the `storage_token`'s `allowed_scopes` claim.

params.name: path
params.summary: Same logical path you passed to `files/upload_begin` (re-validated server-side).
notes: Looked up via `(scope, owner, path)` with a row lock (`SELECT … FOR UPDATE`).
If the row is missing or not in `mode='object'` → `STORAGE_ERR_NOT_FOUND` (`-32022`).

If the row exists but the `__pending` flag was already cleared (re-finalize after success, or a `path` that was never started via `upload_begin`) → `STORAGE_ERR_NOT_FOUND` ("object not pending finalize"). Finalize is **not** idempotent — call it exactly once per begin.

params.name: etag
params.summary: ETag you read from the presigned `PUT` response. **Stored but not verified** by APS.
notes: Despite the field name, APS does **not** compare your `etag` to the stored object's ETag — it queries the object directly and uses the canonical APS-computed ETag (truncated to 64 chars). Pass it anyway for parity with the SDK signature and forward-compat.
If APS cannot verify the uploaded object (it never landed, wrong key, transient object-store outage) the call raises `pending_upload`, surfaced by the host as `STORAGE_ERR_UPSTREAM` (`-32029`).
ETag length is capped at 64 chars — APS truncates rather than rejecting.

params.name: size_bytes
params.summary: Actual uploaded size — **advisory**. APS uses its own measured size, not yours.
notes: Quota reconciliation compares the APS-measured object size to the entry's stored `size_bytes` (the value you declared at `upload_begin`). Positive diff → hard-reserve from quota (may raise `STORAGE_ERR_QUOTA_EXCEEDED`); negative diff → refund.
Your `size_bytes` argument here is **not used** for reconciliation; only kept on the signature for SDK convenience. Tracking your local byte count is still useful for logs.

params.name: content_type
params.summary: Forwarded to Nexus but **silently dropped** by the current REST schema.
notes: `_FilesFinalizeBody` only declares `path` / `etag` / `size_bytes` / `metadata`; FastAPI ignores extra fields. To change `content_type` after finalize there is no supported call — re-upload from scratch.

params.name: timeout
params.summary: SDK-side per-call deadline in seconds (default 60s).
notes: Independent of the Agent → APS HTTP timeout (15s) and APS's own verification budget. Bumping this does not lift the upstream limits.

returns.desc:
Verbatim `ObjectEntry` body from Nexus — the durable, post-finalize row:
• `path: str` — canonicalised logical path.
• `etag: str` — **canonical APS-computed object ETag** (truncated to 64 chars); use as `if_match` for subsequent `files/delete`.
• `generation: int` — bumped on every successful finalize (begin → 1, finalize → 2 for a fresh upload).
• `size_bytes: int` — **actual** APS-measured object size, may differ from your declared value.
• `content_type: str | None` — as set at `upload_begin`.
• `metadata: dict` — with `__pending` removed and any `metadata=` you passed here merged in (server-side `md.update(metadata)`).
• `tags: list[str] | None` — as set at `upload_begin`.
• `updated_at: str` — ISO-8601 timestamp.

errors.name: STORAGE_ERR_INVALID_REQUEST

errors.name: STORAGE_ERR_NOT_FOUND
errors.desc: Key/path does not exist (normalised on `get`).

errors.name: STORAGE_ERR_PRECONDITION_FAILED
errors.desc: if_match ETag did not match current generation.

errors.name: STORAGE_ERR_UPSTREAM

items.example:
# Idiomatic finalize after a successful presigned PUT (full flow lives on `files/upload_begin`).
from executa_sdk import ctx

async def finalize_after_put(path: str, put_response) -> dict:
    obj_etag = put_response.headers["etag"].strip('"')
    entry = await ctx.storage.files.upload_complete(
        path=path,
        etag=obj_etag,                          # stored verbatim; advisory only
        size_bytes=len(put_response.request.content),  # advisory; APS is source of truth
    )
    # entry == {'path': ..., 'etag': '<canonical-aps-etag>', 'generation': 2,
    #           'size_bytes': 1234, 'content_type': 'application/pdf', ...}
    return entry
limitations: **Not idempotent**: calling `files/upload_complete` twice on the same path raises `STORAGE_ERR_NOT_FOUND` because the second call finds no `__pending` row. Build retry logic around the begin → PUT → complete trio, not the complete call in isolation.

**Must run after the presigned `PUT` lands**: if APS attempts verification before the object is visible (transient propagation, retried upload) you get a `pending_upload` error mapped to `STORAGE_ERR_UPSTREAM` (`-32029`). Retry the `complete` call after a short backoff; the entry stays pending and the URL stays valid until its TTL.

**Your `etag` is logged but not verified** — supplying a wrong/empty value still succeeds. Real integrity is APS's measured object size at verification time; treat the returned `etag` as authoritative.

**Quota can fail late**: if your actual upload is larger than the declared `size_bytes`, the hard-reserve at finalize may raise `STORAGE_ERR_QUOTA_EXCEEDED` *after* the bytes are already uploaded. The orphan object is retained by APS infrastructure (not counted toward your APS quota) and is not auto-cleaned. Always honour `size_bytes` honestly at `upload_begin`.
**Cannot mutate `content_type` after the fact** — the finalize schema ignores it. Choose the right MIME type at `upload_begin`.
**`metadata=` is merged, not replaced** (server does `md.update(metadata)`), in contrast to `storage/set` semantics. To clear a metadata key you must re-upload.
Requires manifest permission `storage.write` and a `storage_token` whose `allowed_scopes` includes the chosen `scope`. Failure → `STORAGE_ERR_NOT_GRANTED` (`-32021`).

items.name: files/download_url
items.summary: Mint a short-lived presigned `GET` URL for a previously finalised object. The plugin (or the end user, if you hand the URL back) fetches the bytes **directly from APS object storage** — the agent host never proxies the body.
items.signature: downloadurl(*, scope: Literal['user','app','tool'] = 'app', path: str, ttl_seconds: int = 300, expires_in: int | None = None, timeout: float = 60.0) -> dict

params.name: scope
params.summary: ACL scope — must match the scope under which the object was uploaded.
notes: Per-scope access is gated by the `storage_token`'s `allowed_scopes` claim.
Cross-scope lookups are impossible: rows are namespaced by `(scope, owner, path)`.

params.name: path
params.summary: Logical file path (re-validated server-side by `validate_path`).
notes: Looked up via `(scope, owner, path)`; missing row → `STORAGE_ERR_NOT_FOUND` (`-32022`).
Row must be finalised — if it is still `__pending=true` (begin happened, complete didn't) the call raises `pending_upload` mapped to `STORAGE_ERR_UPSTREAM` (`-32029`).
Invalid path syntax → `STORAGE_ERR_INVALID_PATH` (`-32027`).

params.name: expires_in
params.summary: **Currently a no-op via the SDK** — the REST endpoint reads `ttl`, not `expires_in`.
notes: Nexus query parameter is `ttl: int = Query(300, ge=1, le=3600)`. The SDK forwards your value as `?expires_in=...`, which FastAPI silently ignores; the URL always lives **300 s** (5 min) until the SDK is updated.
Hard cap on the server is **3600 s** (1 h). Calling the REST endpoint directly with `?ttl=N` is the only way to override today.
If you need long-lived sharing, mint a fresh URL on demand rather than caching one.

params.name: timeout
params.summary: SDK-side per-call deadline in seconds (default 60s).
notes: Independent of the 15s Agent→Nexus HTTP timeout; this only bounds the SDK wait.

returns.desc:
Verbatim `PresignedGet` body from Nexus — every field present:
• `get_url: str` — presigned APS `GET` URL. Plain HTTP GET, no auth headers needed; browser-friendly.
• `expires_at: str` — ISO-8601 wall-clock expiry (= server `utcnow()` + `ttl_seconds`). After this, APS rejects the request with 403.
• `etag: str` — canonical APS-computed object ETag (truncated to 64 chars). Use as a client-side cache key.
• `size_bytes: int` — durable size of the object as recorded at finalize.
• `content_type: str | None` — as set at `upload_begin`; pass to your HTTP layer for MIME hints.

Note: the SDK docstring advertises `{"url", "expires_at"}` — the real shape is the richer `PresignedGet` above. Use the documented key `get_url`, not `url`.

items.example:
# Hand a short-lived download link to the user via a sampling reply.
from executa_sdk import ctx

async def share_report(path: str = "reports/q1.pdf") -> str:
    info = await ctx.storage.files.download_url(path=path, scope="app")
    # info == {'get_url': 'https://…/aps-object-download/…?<signature>',
    #          'expires_at': '2026-05-24T12:05:00', 'etag': '…',
    #          'size_bytes': 12345, 'content_type': 'application/pdf'}
    return (
        f"Your report is ready ({info['size_bytes']} bytes, "
        f"expires {info['expires_at']}):\n{info['get_url']}"
    )
limitations: **TTL is locked at 300 s via the SDK** (see `expires_in` notes). For longer URLs hit `GET /api/v1/storage/files/url?ttl=...` directly with the `storage_token`.

**Pending objects return an error**: if `files/upload_complete` has not landed, `download_url` raises `pending_upload` (surfaces as `STORAGE_ERR_UPSTREAM`). Don't expose the URL until finalize succeeds.
**No range / partial download knobs** at this layer — the presigned URL itself supports standard HTTP `Range` requests.
**`disposition` (Content-Disposition) is supported by the REST endpoint** but not exposed by the SDK. Call the REST endpoint directly if you need `attachment; filename=...`.
**Soft-deleted entries are invisible** — once `files/delete` runs, `download_url` returns `STORAGE_ERR_NOT_FOUND` even if the underlying APS object is still retained.
**URL is a bearer credential**: anyone who sees `get_url` until `expires_at` can read the bytes. Treat it like a short-lived password — don't log it, don't embed it in long-lived client state.
Requires manifest permission `storage.read` and a `storage_token` whose `allowed_scopes` covers the requested `scope`.

items.name: files/list
items.summary: Enumerate finalised objects under a path prefix in the plugin's APS Files namespace (alphabetical by `path`, cursor-paginated). Returns metadata heads only — to download the bytes call `files/download_url` per entry.
items.signature: list(*, scope: Literal['user','app','tool'] = 'app', prefix: str | None = None, cursor: str | None = None, limit: int | None = None, timeout: float = 60.0) -> dict

params.name: scope
params.summary: ACL scope — same semantics as `files/upload_begin`. Files default to `app`.
notes: Listing is per-scope; the same path under `tool` and `app` is reported separately if you list each scope.
Per-scope access is gated by the `storage_token`'s `allowed_scopes` claim (`user` / `app` / `tool`).

params.name: prefix
params.summary: Forward-match filter on `path`. Empty (or `None`) lists everything in the scope.
notes: Validated loosely (length ≤ 1024, must not start with `/`); unlike `validate_path` the segments **may** be empty, so trailing `/` like `prefix='reports/'` works.
Forward-match only — no glob/regex/suffix search. Matching is byte-wise on the raw path.
SQL `LIKE` with backslash-escaped wildcards — caller-supplied `%` / `_` characters are matched literally, not as wildcards.

params.name: cursor
params.summary: Opaque continuation token returned by a previous call as `next_cursor`.
notes: Encodes the last-seen path; pages walk strict ascending order (`path > cursor`).
Treat as opaque — do not parse, persist long-term, or share across scopes/prefixes.
Pass `None` (or omit) for the first page.

params.name: limit
params.summary: Page size, **1 .. 1000** (default 100).
notes: Out-of-range values raise `STORAGE_ERR_INVALID_PATH` (`-32027`) at the service layer; the REST endpoint also rejects with HTTP 422 via `Query(100, ge=1, le=1000)`.
The server fetches `limit + 1` rows to decide whether `next_cursor` is set; cost is O(limit).
When the SDK omits this, Nexus picks the server default of 100.

params.name: timeout
params.summary: SDK-side per-call deadline in seconds (default 60s).
notes: Independent of the 15s Agent→Nexus HTTP timeout.

returns.desc:
**`{items: [...], next_cursor: str | None}`**

Each item is an `ObjectListItem` **head only** (no bytes, no download URL):
• `path: str` — logical path of the object.
• `etag: str` — canonical APS-computed object ETag (≤ 64 chars).
• `size_bytes: int` — actual stored size.
• `content_type: str | None` — as set at `upload_begin`.
• `metadata: dict` — with internal flags (`__pending`, `__reservation_token`) already stripped by `upload_complete`.
• `tags: list[str] | None`.
• `updated_at: str` — ISO-8601 timestamp of the last finalize.

`next_cursor` is `None` on the final page. Call `files/download_url` for any path you actually want to read.

limitations: **Heads only** — no `get_url` is included. Listing + downloading N objects is N+1 round-trips. For bulk export, fan-out `download_url` after the list completes.

**Pending uploads are included** in the listing — the row is created at `upload_begin` with `__pending=true`, and the list query does not filter on that flag (only the `mode` and `is_deleted` columns are checked). If you need a clean view, filter client-side on `metadata['__pending']` being absent. (This differs from `download_url`, which rejects pending rows.)
**Ordering is strict ascending `path`** — no reverse, no order-by-`updated_at`, no size/tag filtering server-side. Sort/filter client-side after the page returns.
**Hard page-size cap of 1000**. Full enumeration of a large namespace requires looping on `next_cursor`; expect O(n / page_size) round-trips.
**Soft-deleted entries are excluded** (`is_deleted=True` rows are filtered out at the SQL level).

**Point-in-time per page** — concurrent uploads/deletes between pages can cause an entry to appear twice or be skipped. For an exact snapshot, write a manifest object under a stable path and update it transactionally.
Requires manifest permission `storage.read` and a `storage_token` whose `allowed_scopes` covers the requested `scope`.

items.name: files/delete
items.summary: Soft-delete one finalised object from the plugin's APS Files namespace. The entry is tombstoned (`is_deleted=True`), the byte quota is **immediately** released, and the entry vanishes from `files/list` / `files/download_url`. The underlying APS object is kept for retention until a reaper job purges it.
items.signature: delete(*, scope: Literal['user','app','tool'] = 'app', path: str, timeout: float = 60.0) -> dict

params.name: scope
params.summary: ACL scope — must match the scope under which the object was uploaded.
notes: Cross-scope deletes are impossible: rows are namespaced by `(scope, owner, path)`.
Requires manifest `storage.write`. Per-scope access is gated by the `storage_token`'s `allowed_scopes` claim.

params.name: path
params.summary: Exact logical path to delete (re-validated server-side).
notes: Exact match only — no glob / prefix delete. To bulk-remove, page through `files/list(prefix=…)` and call `files/delete` per path.

Missing or wrong-mode row → `STORAGE_ERR_NOT_FOUND` (`-32022`). Unlike `files/download_url`, **pending uploads can be deleted** — the row is dropped and the soft reservation is released by Redis after its TTL.

params.name: timeout
params.summary: SDK-side per-call deadline in seconds (default 60s).
notes: Independent of the 15s Agent→Nexus HTTP timeout.

returns.desc:
**`{deleted: True}`** — synthesised by the Matrix storage handler from Nexus's `{ok: true, path: ...}` envelope (`_postprocess` collapses success bodies to a uniform shape across KV and Files deletes).

Always returns `deleted=True` on success; no etag/generation/path is echoed back (the row is tombstoned, not rewritten). Re-read with `files/list` to confirm absence.

limitations: **Soft delete only** — the entry is flagged `is_deleted=True` and `deleted_at` is stamped; the underlying APS object is retained until the platform-side retention reaper runs. Do not rely on this call for security-grade or compliance-grade wipes — contact platform support if you need hard deletion before retention elapses.
**Quota is released immediately** (the byte count is subtracted from `used_bytes` and `entries_count` is decremented). Re-uploading the same path right after a delete will not double-count.
**Deleting a missing path raises `STORAGE_ERR_NOT_FOUND`** — unlike the SDK's KV `delete` wording, 404 is not normalised here. Wrap in try/except if you cannot pre-check.

**No CAS via the SDK** — even though the REST endpoint accepts `if_match`, `FilesClient.delete` does not forward it. Concurrent overwrite + delete races can tombstone a row that another caller just finalised; if that matters, fall through to the REST endpoint directly.
**No bulk / glob delete**. Iterate `files/list(prefix=…)` + `files/delete` to clear a namespace; expect O(n) round-trips.
**Takes a Postgres row lock** (`SELECT … FOR UPDATE`). Concurrent deletes on the same path serialise — the loser sees `STORAGE_ERR_NOT_FOUND`.
Requires manifest `storage.write` and a `storage_token` whose `allowed_scopes` covers the requested `scope`.
